plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the weakly dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies. Bidding higher than my value risks winning and paying more than the item is worth if others bid between my value and my bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to inform deviation, I'll bid exactly my value of $31.

In a second-price auction, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. This ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest competing bid, and my profit is maximized without risk of overpaying, since I only pay the second-highest bid regardless of how high my own bid is. Bidding above value risks negative profit if I win at a price above my value; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $6, bidding $6 is optimal.

My value for this item is $0. Since profit = value - price paid if I win, any positive payment would result in a loss. The only way to guarantee non-negative profit is to bid $0, ensuring I either lose (profit $0) or in the rare case I "win" at $0, I still pay $0 and profit $0. There's no benefit to bidding higher since any positive value has no upside for me.
